subject: Reserved commit, throughput verification protocol, and discount pathway
messages:
From: Rachel Torres <rachel.torres@datafin.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: ops@datafin.com, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-09-30T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Dedicated capacity — throughput guarantees & discount ask

Hi Marcus,

Thanks for the demo last week — DataFin is interested in moving from a trial to a 12-month reserved commit for dedicated capacity. Before we pull legal in, I need clarity on three items so we can finalize internal approval: 

1) Throughput guarantees — you list tokens/sec in the proposal and our infra team thinks requests/sec (rps) is a better operational metric for our gateway. Can you explain how Redwood maps tokens/sec to rps for multi-turn chat? What measurement windows do you use?

2) Latency targets — we need P95 latency targets for both short (<=64 tokens) and long (>=512 tokens) responses. We also need to know what counts as a violation (network jitter vs model stall).

3) Discount pathing — given a 12-month commit and a requirement for guaranteed throughput (sustained), what level of discount can we expect? If we agree to a verification run and sizing constraints, can pricing move from the self-serve tier to a reserved-commit price?

I've attached our expected workload sample (ops@datafin.com sent traces) and will share anonymized request logs if useful. Can you propose a measurement protocol we can sign off on?

Appreciate a short written reply and a proposed next step.

— Rachel
Rachel Torres
Head of Platform Engineering, DataFin Analytics
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: Rachel Torres <rachel.torres@datafin.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-09-30T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity — throughput guarantees & discount ask

Rachel,

Thanks — great to hear DataFin is ready to commit. I put together a concise proposal and attached two artifacts: a measurement_protocol_v1.xlsx (walkthrough + data template) and an initial pricing_offer_DF-2026-4237.xlsx. Summary below.

Throughput mapping (tokens/sec vs rps)
- Tokens/sec is our core billing/throughput metric because it aligns with model compute. For multi-turn chat we report both tokens/sec and an equivalent rps using a workload-weighted average: rps = total_requests / measurement_window_seconds.
- For sizing we run a 20-minute steady-state window and a 10-minute burst window. Steady-state gives the committed throughput; burst handles short spikes.

Latency SLOs
- Proposed targets (P95): short responses (<=64 tokens): 110ms; long responses (>=512 tokens): 420ms.
- We separate transport/network variance (packet loss/retries) from model time by measuring from request receipt at our edge to final token emitted by the model (redwood_edge_receive -> model_emit). Network-only anomalies (upstream ISP outages) are excluded via health checks.

Discount pathway
- For a 12-month reserved commit with a 6-month ramp to full utilization and a verified sizing run, we can offer a committed-capacity discount of 18% off list for the baseline pool, plus negotiated volume bands for overage. If DataFin can commit to a larger minimum GPU pool (>=8 A100-equivalent), we can extend to 22%. The pricing sheet shows tier breakpoints.

Next steps
- If that aligns, sign the measurement protocol and share a 72-hour anonymized trace. We'll schedule a 2-week verification run where we execute the measurement windows and provide a throughput/latency report.

LMK a good time for a 30-min call tomorrow to review the runbook — I can invite Dev (our platform PM) to explain sizing assumptions.

Best,
Marcus Lin
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-01T08:15:00-07:00
Subject: Fw: Dedicated capacity — throughput guarantees & discount ask

Marcus / Dev — looping you in with my read on the ask. Key constraints: DataFin expects dual metrics (tokens/sec and rps) and strict P95s. They want discount movement to 22% if they commit to >=8 GPU pool.

Operational notes for proposal:
- Measurement run: require a 10% baseline offset to be conservative (they must achieve 90% of declared steady-state for commit to be validated).
- Burst policy: allow 30% burst above steady-state for 10 minutes before throttling — explain in SOW.
- Validation data: need anonymized request-level traces plus sequence-length distribution.

Pricing flexibility: finance prefers 18% for standard 12mo unless legal adds more risk clauses. We can approve 22% only if legal signs off on a strict validation acceptance criteria and an SLA credit schedule.

I'll draft a short internal note for legal and finance. Marcus — can you push the measurement_protocol_v1.xlsx to the shared drive with the trace template? Dev — estimate GPU pool sizing for their trace and comment on how many A100-eq units map to their 90th percentile tokens/sec.

- Laura
Director, Enterprise Sales Operations
From: Rachel Torres <rachel.torres@datafin.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: ops@datafin.com, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-03T11:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity — throughput guarantees & discount ask

Marcus, Laura — thanks for the clear breakdown. Couple of clarifications before we commit: 

- Can Redwood reduce the short-response target to P95 100ms? Our SLA reviewers prefer round numbers and tighter latency for small replies. Is that achievable without moving them to a higher-tier pool?
- We agree to provide anonymized traces. For the verification run, we want an on-prem-style validation (you run the test against a mirrored workload from our staging gateway). Can you outline the ops steps and whether Redwood will require VPN or a short-lived peering?
- If we hit the acceptance criteria in the verification window, we expect the 22% pricing to be applied retroactively to the start of the committed term. Is that acceptable?

I'll attach our current purchase terms (SOW_draft.pdf) for redline.

— Rachel
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: Rachel Torres <rachel.torres@datafin.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-05T16:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity — throughput guarantees & discount ask

Rachel — thanks, all reasonable asks. Quick answers and next steps: 

1) Short-response P95 at 100ms: we can commit to 100ms P95 for <=64 tokens only if the verified pool is sized to handle your 90th-percentile concurrency without relying on burst credits. That will likely require the >=8 A100-eq pool you referenced. Dev will send an estimate for the trace you provided by EOD Monday.

2) Verification run ops: standard approach is mirrored staging traffic to our private peering or a secure tunneled collector — we support both. For peering we need an IP allowlist and a short peering NAT; for tunneled collector we provide a short-lived mutually authenticated TLS endpoint. We'll include the detailed ops checklist in the runbook. No persistent VPN required for the typical flow.

3) Retroactive pricing: we can apply the 22% price if the verification run meets acceptance criteria and legal signs the validation annex within 10 business days of the run. We'll add explicit language in the SOW draft (I attached a redline-ready SOW_draft.pdf back).

Next steps:
- Dev to estimate pool sizing (EOD Monday).
- Marcus to share the measurement_protocol_v1.xlsx template and a short runbook excerpt; schedule 30-min runbook review with your ops next Tue.
- Legal/Finance: Laura will follow up with a one-pager of the validation acceptance criteria we need in the SOW.

I'll set the runbook call — suggested time Tue 10am PT.

Best,
Marcus
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
